about: synthetic@PrompTugal.dinis's findings ledger (at Dinis Cruz's word, 6 November 2026: every finding is seen and gets a decision, even when the decision is not to act). One row per fix sent to an owner. The owner sets status to accepted, declined (with why), later or done in its own commit at its next wake; synthetic@ re-measures and sets verified, or re-opens with evidence. The findings page shows what waits on whom.

statuses.declined: the owner will not, with why
statuses.done: the owner says it is live

items.finding: The £ credit pill and per-page meter are never explained; every persona read it as a paywall or a charge, the founder as pay-to-be-featured.
items.evidence: run 5: all 4 again; the balance drops on opening a story (£5.00 to £4.92..4.98) and is back on About; "read 0%" or "5%" after a full read; run 6: the mock-ups keep "£5.00 credit" unexplained (Ana, Miguel)

items.finding: No way to reach a person or send a correction on company pages or About ('Tell us' has no link); waits on the editors' address from Dinis.
Company pages say the team keeps notes on 'whether to meet, who owns it': read as a sales pipeline (runs 1, 3, 4: the line that did most against).
Company pages say 'We have not asked <company> yet', false the day the email lands.
The mandate ('to map the universe of AI in Portugal') on no page.
items.evidence: front page and About, v0.1.77 (run 4) and v0.1.86

items.finding: About is stale: 'the writing desks are next', 'Vicky, editor', 'no human review first' with no statement of what a human reviews.
items.evidence: run 5: About still says "the writing desks are next" and "Vicky"; no press contact; does not say whether a human reviews each article

items.finding: For Dinis: what RiskMandate is, who owns it, whether it sells to the companies covered; whether answers are optional, approved before publication, never used for sales.
Tailor the ask to the kind of organisation (bank, fund, media do not run agents in that sense).

items.evidence: draft 01:00 UTC: 'por agora, a página está em inglês' (run 2)

items.evidence: run 5 (v0.1.90): 7 of 11 articles scroll sideways on a 390 px phone (591, 591, 480, 429, 417, 405, 399 px); the agent block is cut ("oper", "instru")

items.finding: Front page: no 'first time? start here' entry; the first-day guide is sixth in Latest.
Data that contradicts itself on one page (AICEP confirmed and 404; Startup Portugal 'no summit page'; Air Apps 'United States' under Portuguese startups); 'conferenceSlug lis26' shown to readers.
For investors: no stage, founders or stand; 'companies we follow' mixes agencies with startups.
Bylines read as agent addresses; a reporter wants the human editor's name and whether they read it before it went live.

items.finding: 'OUR PICK' beside 'Nothing on it is an endorsement'.
The footer's 'Source code' links the old SGit-AI repository.
Image syntax in the content markdown, so pages can show screenshots (now: a vault gallery, F27).
'powered by RiskMandate' with no line on what it is; no greeting; 'mandato' blurs mission and question.

items.finding: For Dinis: the disclosure's 'This is not independent coverage. We may write about companies the team hopes to meet or sell to' stops a comms lead passing the email to leaders. Not a case for softening it: what is the commercial relation, and can the email say it plainly?
The email's disclosure was softer than the page it links.
Nothing says who reads PrompTugal.news or how it is funded.
Flows print 'The agent: ... Agent: ...' on every agent step.
items.evidence: 1Password page, v0.1.86: the marker reads as where an AI agent acts

items.finding: A source URL cut at a hyphen reads as a broken link.
items.evidence: 1Password page, v0.1.86: cut URLs end with an ellipsis

items.finding: Sources name a speaker ('may be a past-edition highlight') while People says 'No one is listed'.
No line that the 15 minutes is not a sales conversation and nobody from RiskMandate is in it (the comms director's one change, twice); for Dinis via the conductor.
'Powered by RiskMandate' on company pages' masthead kept the page from a leader; brand, Dinis's call.

A vault gallery: the findings page shows the screenshots from the synthetic vault (desks/synthetic/vault.json, read key published) with the site's own vault-embed.js, as /newsroom/observability/ reads its vault; the repository no longer carries them.

'Signed' is only a word: no article links its signature (served at articles/<slug>.md.sig) or the key (board/keys.json), or says in one line what a reader can do with it. All 4 readers in run 5 guessed what it means; none could check it. The site's strongest provenance claim is the one nobody could use.
items.evidence: run 6: "signed" still unexplained in the mock-ups (Ana, Miguel)

items.finding: The provenance blocks are not explained: the code box at the end has no heading (read as machine metadata, cut on the phone), and the plain-text link reads as 'only for machines'. One line each on what they are for and how a reader uses them.

'Who made this' uses insider words: 'storyline S2', 'the curator's map', 'marked Ready', 'Vicky's reviewer', 'desks/curator/README.md', '403' (20 occurrences across the articles). The chain itself worked (Miguel read it as a CI pipeline); its words lost Ana, Helena and Tom.
Europe in Pavilion 4: 'In short' says Henna Virkkunen speaks on Centre Stage on 10 November, without the caveat (Web Summit's speakers page, as read, does not list her) that comes two screens later.

The homepage's second screen is an attendee agenda: Ana, Helena and Tom concluded the site is only for people going to the summit. The nav's '£5.00', 'Vault', 'Ask', 'Paper' controls have no labels for a first visit.
Source URLs print raw in angle brackets, break mid-word on the phone and do not look tappable.
Lisbon's universities: 'Unitree G02' vs 'G1', and 'for this draft' in published text, confused the student.

The front-page mock-ups (A, B, C) change the bylines to 'Vicky Wang's desk' or 'PrompTugal.news', so work written by an AI agent reads as written by a person (Helena, Tom; measured on A's first screen). Run 5's readers asked for both: the AI agent that wrote it and the human editor accountable.

All three mock-ups move what makes the site different to the bottom ('Why we are different') and shrink 'Every fact sourced' to one grey line; today's page shows it first. Helena ranked today above every mock-up for that reason; Tom: 'today's page wins on trust'.

The AI-made lead infographic cannot be read on a phone, and its figures are doubted (Ana, Miguel, Helena, Tom); its 'DATES: 8 to 13 November 2026' are the Brazilian mission's own dates (sourced in the article) but sit under a Web Summit headline, so two readers took them for the summit's (9 to 12) and called it wrong. Label them as the mission's.

B, the visual wall, was ranked last by all four: bare figures ('84%', 'Up to 125') with no source beside them read as marketing (Miguel, Helena), no story leads (Tom), text too small on a phone (Ana).

C's briefing ('Before the summit, in 30 seconds') was Ana's and Miguel's favourite, but its three claims carry no source or author (Helena, Miguel), and 'Play the briefing' does not say what it plays.

Today's front page lists 'Registration: collect your lanyard and wristband' three times under the same title (the airport, Pavilhão de Portugal), which reads as a duplicate; the place belongs in the title.
